notices.short_title: ELECTRICAL UNIT - SOLAR AND PY TRAINING

notices.description: NYCEM has identified the need and is seeking to purchase New Intercoms & Access Control for the Security System at the NYCEM ESC. This procurement will piggyback off of an existing OGS contract (NYS PT68745).
notices.plain: New York City Emergency Management awarded A+ Technology & Security Solutions Inc. a $47,098 contract for new intercoms and access control for its security system, bought through an existing New York State Office of General Services contract.

notices.short_title: BWS Removal, Transport, Dispose of Waste 6016011X
notices.plain: The Department of Environmental Protection awarded ENP Environmental Inc a $761,676 contract for removing, transporting and disposing of waste for its Bureau of Water Supply, using a noncompetitive small purchase from a certified minority- or women-owned business.

The Department of Environmental Protection awarded Heredia Gonzalez Inc a $282,433 contract for uniforms, using a small purchase from a certified minority- or women-owned business without competition.
The Fire Department awarded Central Lake Armor Express Inc a $32,960 contract to buy ballistic vests through an Intergovernmental Purchase, meaning a contract another government already holds.

notices.short_title: Inspection Services at Asphalt and Concrete Plants Citywide
notices.plain: The Department of Transportation awarded Twin Peaks Inc a $1,887,832 contract, chosen from competing proposals, for inspection services at asphalt and concrete plants citywide.

notices.description: Cornerstone Community Centers provide engaging activities year-round for young people and adults. Programs are located at 99 New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) Community Centers throughout the five boroughs, and were shaped by input from young people, NYCHA residents, Resident Association leaders, elected officials, and principals at schools that serve youth who live in the participating developments.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Brooklyn Bureau of Community Service an $8.2 million negotiated contract to run Cornerstone Community Centers, which offer year-round activities for young people and adults at 99 New York City Housing Authority community centers across the five boroughs.

notices.short_title: Capacity Building MWBE for Cultivating Partnerships Renewal
notices.description: This solicitation is being made pursuant to the M/WBE Noncompetitive Small Purchase Method, Section 3-08 of the New York City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, this procurement is exclusively for the City Certified Minority and Woman Owned Business (M/WBEs). Contracts awarded under this method may not exceed $500,000, inclusive of any and all change orders, overruns, amendments, renewals and extensions. Through this solicitation, The Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD) is seeking an appropriately qualified vendor to support small and emerging community-based organizations, including faith-based organizations, to better serve their communities through networking with other community leaders and established organizations, and provide connections to consultants and mentoring institutions as appropriate.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development renewed a $300,000 contract with J Jackson Consulting LLC, a certified minority- or women-owned business, to help small and emerging community groups, including faith-based organizations, build networks and connect with consultants and mentors.

The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Henry Street Settlement a $6.3 million contract for elementary-school COMPASS center-based programs in Manhattan's District 3 (the notice's "Manhattan 03"), chosen from competing proposals among vendors approved in advance.

To support CBOs in a variety of activities focused on structuring organizational policies and practices to promote anti-racism and build and enhance approaches to equity. Contracts awarded under this method may not exceed $500,000, inclusive of any and all change orders, overruns, amendments, renewals and extensions.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development renewed a $450,000 contract with Equity and Community LLC, a minority- or women-owned business, to help community-based organizations develop anti-racism and equity policies and practices.

notices.short_title: COMPASS Center Based - Bronx 02, 05, Mn 10, & Qn 12 Middle
notices.description: COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs. Awarded for COMPASS Center-Based - Bronx -CD 2 -991 Longwood Avenue, Bronx, NY 10459, Bronx CD-5 - 2255 Webster Avenue, Bronx, NY 10457 - Manhattan CD-10 - 441 Manhattan Avenue, New York, NY 10026 - Queens CD-12 -116-25 Guy R Brewer Boulvard Queens, NY 11434
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Police Athletic League Inc a $6,364,440 contract to run COMPASS after-school, summer and holiday youth programs at four middle school sites in the Bronx, Manhattan and Queens.

notices.agency_name: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
notices.description:
Notice of Concept Paper

The NYC Department of Social Service (DSS)/Human Resources Administration (HRA) is committed to strengthening and modernizing the NYCBenefits Program to promote accountability, workforce capacity, cross-system coordination, and high-quality, client-centered services. The purpose of this document is to:
 

  1. Outline HRAs proposed enhancements to the NYCBenefits service model;
  2. Solicit stakeholder feedback regarding program design and operational requirements;
  3. Assess provider interest and organizational capacity; and
  4. Inform the development of a Request for Proposals (RFP)/RFx.

Anticipated number of contracts: Between thirty-eight (38) and fifty-eight (58), aligned with the following provider specializations:
 

  • Thirty-five (35) to fifty-three (53) Direct service vendors
  • Three (3) to five (5) Technical Assistance vendors


Anticipated annual funding: $9,750,0000 to $14,950,000 over the three (3) year contract term (approximately $300-$350 per client), subject to funding availability.
